headline: Student power protests in Dhaka against attack on NCP march in Habiganj
summary: Members of Jatiya Chhatra Shakti held a rally at Dhaka University to demand the arrest of those involved in the attack on National Citizens Party leaders.
details: The student wing of the National Citizens Party (NCP), Jatiya Chhatra Shakti, held a protest march and rally in Dhaka on Wednesday night to condemn an attack on the party's July march in Habiganj.
The protest began at the TSC Payra Chattar of Dhaka University, moving through the VC square and ending at the Raju sculpture, where a short assembly was held.
Protesters alleged that members of Chhatra Dal and Jubo Dal were involved in the attack in Habiganj and demanded the immediate arrest of the perpetrators based on video evidence.
Abu Baker Majumdar, Central General Secretary of Jatiya Chhatra Shakti, criticized Tarique Rahman, claiming that the party's current strategy is to silence people and attack meetings and rallies.
Majumdar further claimed that NCP leaders were blocked by trucks in Habiganj to suppress them politically, though the NCP managed to move the empty trucks themselves.
Tahmid Al Muddassir Chowdhury, DU branch president of the organization, compared the tactics used to block the NCP march to those used by the former government to suppress dissent.
The rally was attended by leaders and activists from Dhaka University, various private universities, and several colleges.
caption:
Students take to the streets in Dhaka to condemn an attack on NCP leaders in Habiganj. They demand immediate arrests of those involved.

The student wing of the National Citizens Party (NCP), Jatiya Chhatra Shakti, held a protest march and rally in Dhaka on Wednesday night to condemn an attack on the party's July march in Habiganj.

The protest began at the TSC Payra Chattar of Dhaka University, moving through the VC square and ending at the Raju sculpture, where a short assembly was held.

Protesters alleged that members of Chhatra Dal and Jubo Dal were involved in the attack in Habiganj and demanded the immediate arrest of the perpetrators based on video evidence.

Abu Baker Majumdar, Central General Secretary of Jatiya Chhatra Shakti, criticized Tarique Rahman, claiming that the party's current strategy is to silence people and attack meetings and rallies.

Majumdar further claimed that NCP leaders were blocked by trucks in Habiganj to suppress them politically, though the NCP managed to move the empty trucks themselves.

Tahmid Al Muddassir Chowdhury, DU branch president of the organization, compared the tactics used to block the NCP march to those used by the former government to suppress dissent.

The rally was attended by leaders and activists from Dhaka University, various private universities, and several colleges.

headline: EC plans presidential polls likely in late August
summary: The Election Commission has begun preparations to elect a new head of state following the resignation of President Mohammed Shahabuddin.
details: The Election Commission (EC) is planning to hold the presidential election in the last week of August to elect the new head of state.
The move comes after President Mohammed Shahabuddin resigned on July 24, with Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad currently serving as acting president.
According to the constitution, the EC must hold the election within 90 days of the vacancy. Preliminary discussions have already been place with Acting Speaker Kayser Kamal.
Chief Election Commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin stated that the official schedule will be announced once the voter list of members of parliament is received from the parliament secretariat.
The election process will involve MPs casting their votes in the parliament chamber. If only one valid candidate is declared, they will be elected unopposed.
To contest the election, candidates must be at least 35 years old and qualified to be an MP, requiring a proposer and seconder who are both members of parliament.
On election day, the CEC will preside over the session, and voting will begin after noon. The results will be counted publicly by the CEC.
caption:
A new head of state is coming. The EC is preparing for presidential polls in late August.

The Election Commission (EC) is planning to hold the presidential election in the last week of August to elect the new head of state.

The move comes after President Mohammed Shahabuddin resigned on July 24, with Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad currently serving as acting president.

According to the constitution, the EC must hold the election within 90 days of the vacancy. Preliminary discussions have already been place with Acting Speaker Kayser Kamal.

Chief Election Commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin stated that the official schedule will be announced once the voter list of members of parliament is received from the parliament secretariat.

The election process will involve MPs casting their votes in the parliament chamber. If only one valid candidate is declared, they will be elected unopposed.

To contest the election, candidates must be at least 35 years old and qualified to be an MP, requiring a proposer and seconder who are both members of parliament.

On election day, the CEC will preside over the session, and voting will begin after noon. The results will be counted publicly by the CEC.
